outcome: Obstetric practice patterns (perioperative OB involvement, fetal monitoring practices)
cohort: The study included 72 pregnant patients who underwent ureteroscopy with fellowship-trained endourologists at seven institutions from 2015 to 2024.
finding: Ureteroscopy (URS) is safe during pregnancy for stone disease when performed by experienced urologists, with no cases of preterm labor directly linked to the procedure and early contractions resolving spontaneously, though obstetric management and fetal monitoring practices vary significantly across institutions.
mod_finding: Two cases of preterm labor requiring C-section at 27 weeks were noted, but these were linked to underlying obstetric comorbidities rather than the URS procedure itself.
gest_age: Mean maternal gestational age was 23.5 weeks at the time of URS.
